item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 131119
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Tue Oct 13 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Simon, located about 100 miles west of Cabo Corrientes, Mexico.

South of Southern Mexico (EP93):
Showers and thunderstorms are becoming better organized in
association with an area of low pressure located a few hundred miles
south of the coast of southern Mexico, and recent satellite-derived
wind data indicate that the circulation is becoming better defined.
If current trends continue, advisories will likely be initiated
later today on a tropical depression or tropical storm. The system
is expected to move generally west-northwestward around 10 mph.
Interests in southwestern Mexico should continue to monitor the
progress of this system. For additional information, including Gale
Warnings, see High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather
Service.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...near 100 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...near 100 percent.

&&
High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service can be
found under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN02 KWBC, and on
the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Tropical Depression Twenty-One-e Public Advisory Number 1
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Tue Oct 13 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 131449
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Twenty-One-E Advisory Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
900 AM CST Tue Oct 13 2026
 
...TROPICAL DEPRESSION TWENTY-ONE-E FORMS OFF THE COAST OF SOUTHERN
MEXICO...
...FORECAST TO RAPIDLY INTENSIFY TO A MAJOR HURRICANE OVER THE NEXT
FEW DAYS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 AM CST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...9.8N 96.5W
ABOUT 540 MI...870 KM SSE OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 820 MI...1320 KM SE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 305 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1006 MB...29.71 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.

Interests in southwestern and west-central Mexico should monitor 
the progress of Tropical Depression Twenty-One-E.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 AM CST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression 
Twenty-One-E was located near latitude 9.8 North, longitude 96.5 
West. The depression is moving toward the northwest near 10 mph (17 
km/h). A motion between west-northwest and northwest should continue 
through Wednesday night.  A turn toward the north-northwest and a 
decrease in forward speed is expected on Thursday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Rapid intensification is forecast during the next 3 days, and the 
cyclone is expected to become a hurricane by Wednesday night and a 
major hurricane by Friday.

The estimated minimum central pressure is 1006 mb (29.71 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Tropical Depression Twenty-One-E are 
expected to begin affecting portions of the coast of southern Mexico 
late this week.  These swells are likely to cause life-threatening 
surf and rip current conditions.  Please consult products from your 
local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Depression Twenty-One-e Forecast Discussion Number 1
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Tue Oct 13 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 131453
TCDEP1
 
Tropical Depression Twenty-One-E Discussion Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP212026
900 AM CST Tue Oct 13 2026
 
Satellite images show that the area of low pressure located to the 
south of southern Mexico has become better organized over the past 
24 hours.  Large areas of banded deep convection are seen to the 
north and the east of the low-level center.  An OSCAT pass from 0630 
UTC this morning showed a closed circulation, but it was a bit short 
of being considered well-defined at that time since the data still 
showed a broad and somewhat elongated area of weak winds within 
about 75 n mi of the center.  However, the convective organization 
and curved banding has increased since that time, and the 
circulation appears to have tightened up a bit over the past several 
hours.  The subjective Dvorak estimate from TAFB is T2.0/30 kt, and 
it is estimated that a tropical depression has formed with an 
initial intensity of 30 kt.

The initial motion of Tropical Depression Twenty-One-E is estimated 
to be northwestward, or 305/9 kt.  A west-northwestward to 
northwestward motion should continue over the next 36 hours while a 
mid-level ridge persists over the northwestern Gulf of America.  
Thereafter, a turn to the northwest or north-northwest is likely as 
the ridge weakens.  A decrease in forward speed is also expected 
after day 2 as the cyclone gets caught in weaker steering currents 
in between the weak ridge to its north and Hurricane Simon to its 
northwest.  Spread in the track forecast is larger than normal from 
day 3 to 5, and some of this uncertainty is likely also due to 
uncertainty in Simon's track.  A cold front moving southward from 
Texas into Mexico toward the end of the forecast period could help 
draw Simon closer to the coastline of Mexico, if the front is potent 
enough.  Regardless, Tropical Depression 21-E could potentially be 
very close to the coast of Mexico as a hurricane over the weekend, 
and several Google DeepMind Ensemble members show the cyclone making 
landfall in southwestern or west-central Mexico.  The NHC forecast 
closely follows the HFIP Corrected Consensus Approach (HCCA), and 
isn't too far off from the Google DeepMind Ensemble Mean.  
Confidence in the track forecast is low, especially beyond day 3.

The cyclone is forecast to traverse extremely favorable oceanic and 
atmospheric conditions for at least the next 3 to 4 days.  The NHC 
intensity forecast shows steady strengthening over the next 24 hours 
as the cyclone works to develop a convective core.  After that time, 
rapid intensification is forecast during the 24 to 72 h time window. 
The DTOPS in the ECMWF-based SHIPS guidance is forecasting a 74 
percent chance of a 65-kt increase over the next 72 h.  The NHC 
intensity forecast is even more aggressive and shows 85 knots of 
strengthening over the next 72 h.  The NHC forecast is slightly 
below the HCCA and GDMI in the short term, but very near the HCCA 
and GDMI beyond Day 2.  The HAFS-A and HAFS-B models strengthen the 
cyclone to a category 4, and 36 of the 50 Google DeepMind members 
make it a category 4 or stronger, so the NHC forecast will 
aggressively show this system reaching category 4 strength at days 3 
and 4.  Beyond day 4, the possibility of increasing vertical wind 
shear and land interaction could induce some weakening, and most of 
the guidance shows the system losing some intensity after day 4.  
Confidence in the intensity forecast is above average.  We are 
fairly confident it will become a strong hurricane due to the 
favorable environmental conditions and model guidance.

 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  13/1500Z  9.8N  96.5W   30 KT  35 MPH
 12H  14/0000Z 10.5N  97.6W   40 KT  45 MPH
 24H  14/1200Z 11.3N  99.3W   50 KT  60 MPH
 36H  15/0000Z 12.0N 100.5W   65 KT  75 MPH
 48H  15/1200Z 12.8N 101.4W   80 KT  90 MPH
 60H  16/0000Z 13.7N 101.9W  100 KT 115 MPH
 72H  16/1200Z 14.5N 102.2W  115 KT 130 MPH
 96H  17/1200Z 16.5N 103.5W  120 KT 140 MPH
120H  18/1200Z 18.6N 105.3W  105 KT 120 MPH
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Hurricane Simon Public Advisory Number 25
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Tue Oct 13 2026 
000
WTPZ35 KNHC 131454
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Simon Advisory Number  25
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
800 AM MST Tue Oct 13 2026
 
...SMALL SIMON FORECAST TO MOVE SLOWLY OVER THE NEXT DAY OR TWO...
...INTERESTS IN WEST-CENTRAL MEXICO AND BAJA CALIFORNIA SUR SHOULD
CONTINUE TO MONITOR FORECAST UPDATES...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM MST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.3N 107.3W
ABOUT 105 MI...165 KM W OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
ABOUT 210 MI...335 KM SSW OF MAZATLAN MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...90 MPH...150 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 270 DEGREES AT 2 MPH...4 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...977 MB...28.85 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The government of Mexico has changed the Hurricane Warning to a
Hurricane Watch for Las Islas Marias.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* North of Escuinapa to Bahia Tempehuaya
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Cabo Corrientes to Escuinapa
 
A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere in west-central Mexico and in Baja California
Sur should continue to monitor as changes to watches and warnings
are possible today.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM MST (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Simon was located 
near latitude 20.3 North, longitude 107.3 West. Simon is moving 
toward the west near 2 mph (4 km/h). The hurricane is forecast to 
move very slowly over the next couple of days, followed by an 
eventual turn to the north by late this week. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 90 mph (150 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Fluctuations in intensity are likely over the next few days, 
but Simon is forecast to remain a hurricane through midweek.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 10 miles (20 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles
(75 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 977 mb (28.85 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are possible within the hurricane watch
area for Las Islas Marias on Wednesday, and for mainland Mexico on
Thursday, with tropical storm conditions possible by Wednesday.
Tropical storm conditions are possible within the tropical storm
watch area today or Wednesday.
 
RAINFALL: Simon is expected to produce rainfall totals of 1 to 2
inches with isolated maximum amounts of 3 inches over portions of
the states of Baja California Sur, Nayarit, and Sinaloa by Friday.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: A storm surge is possible near or east where Simon's 
center eventually makes landfall along the Mexican coast. 
 
SURF: Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 1100 AM MST.
Next complete advisory at 200 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Hurricane Simon Forecast Discussion Number 24
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM MST Tue Oct 13 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 130842
TCDEP5
 
Hurricane Simon Discussion Number  24
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
200 AM MST Tue Oct 13 2026
 
Simon remains a very small hurricane. Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) 
data from around 01 UTC showed its compact wind field, with a 5-n-mi 
radius of maximum wind and tropical-storm-force winds that extended 
only 30-40 n mi from the center. Satellite images reveal Simon has 
maintained a small central dense overcast tonight, with a sharper 
edge to the cloud tops on the northeastern side, perhaps the result 
of some vertical wind shear. Given the small size of Simon, it is 
possible that conventional satellite estimates are struggling to 
represent its true intensity. The initial intensity is set at 80 kt, 
which lies in between the latest Dvorak CI number from TAFB (4.5/77 
kt) and the earlier SAR data. 
 
The hurricane is moving slowly northwestward (310/3 kt) around a 
subtropical ridge over the southern United States. During the next 
couple of days, Simon is forecast to become caught in weak steering 
currents between this ridge and another ridge that should build to 
the northwest over the eastern Pacific. As a result, most of the 
track guidance now shows little net motion of the storm through 60 
h, although Simon meanders in several different directions in the 
various global models and ensembles. Given the lack of a clear model 
signal, the new NHC forecast attempts to maintain some continuity by 
using a blend of the latest Google DeepMind, AI-GFS, and ECMWF track 
aids through 72 h. Once again, the trend is slower and farther west 
than the previous prediction. A general northward motion is shown at 
96-120 h as the system (if it survives that long) should become 
steered by a cutoff upper low to its northwest. Needless to say, the 
lack of model agreement makes this a very low confidence forecast.

Simon's intensity forecast is also very challenging and highly 
sensitive to its uncertain track. The small system is forecast to be 
within a generally low shear environment over very warm SSTs for the 
next couple of days. However, the slow forward speed of Simon could 
lead to upwelling of cooler waters, and its proximity to land could 
make it susceptible to intrusions of drier air from mainland Mexico. 
Much of the guidance shows little intensity change or even some 
weakening through midweek, and the NHC forecast remains on the 
higher end of the intensity guidance. By Thursday, the model 
consensus favors more steady weakening through the rest of the 
period due to increased vertical wind shear, and the latter half of 
the NHC forecast has been lowered notably from the previous one.

It is worth emphasizing that this is a very low confidence forecast, 
and interests in west-central Mexico should continue to closely 
monitor the latest updates. Changes to watches and warnings may 
be required later today based on the latest forecast trends.

 
Key Messages:
 
1. Hurricane conditions are likely on Las Islas Marias over the
next day or so, where a Hurricane Warning remains in effect.
 
2. Simon could approach the coast of western Mexico later this 
week at or near hurricane strength, and a Hurricane Watch remains 
in effect for a portion of the area.
 
3. Heavy rainfall associated with Simon will impact portions of 
west-central Mexico over the next few days. This rainfall will 
produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas 
of steep terrain.
 
4. Large swells will affect portions of the southwestern and
west-central coasts of Mexico over the next several days. These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions.
